_meta.title: BondingCurveDynamics — Three New Early-Signal Features
_meta.basis: arXiv:2602.14860 — early-window capital efficiency is #1 graduation predictor
_meta.author: Principal Crypto Quant (Apollo subagent)

fields.name: firstNTrades
fields.description: The first 30 trades ever seen for this token, captured in arrival order and NEVER evicted. Used exclusively for initial_capital_efficiency.

fields.name: vSolAfterTrade10
fields.description: vSolInBondingCurve captured at the moment totalSwapCount transitions from 9→10. Written once, never updated.
fields.note: Set AFTER incrementing totalSwapCount so check is === 10 on the 10th trade.

fields.name: vSolAfterTrade30
fields.description: vSolInBondingCurve at the 30th trade. Written once, never updated.

fields.name: accumulationShapeHistory
fields.description: vSolInBondingCurve snapshots taken every ~5 s, capped at 24 entries (~2 min). Separate from capitalEfficiencyHistory (which stores CE/trade not raw vSol) to avoid aliasing.
fields.addTrade_logic: Sampled in computeFeatures() same as capitalEfficiencyHistory — every 5 s or on each call (whichever is larger granularity fits 24 pts).

fields.name: earlyBuyerTimingHistory
fields.description: Timestamps and sizes of the first 50 buy-only trades. Used to compute inter-arrival regularity (bot proxy) without needing instruction account inspection.
fields.addTrade_logic: if (trade.txType === 'buy' && state.earlyBuyerTimingHistory.length < 50) state.earlyBuyerTimingHistory.push({ timestamp: trade.timestamp, solAmount: trade.solAmount });

fields.name: totalSwapCountLifetime
fields.note: Pass state.totalSwapCount so we know how many trades have been seen overall (for grace period logic).

signal_1_initial_capital_efficiency.rationale: Paper §4: CE computed on the first N trades is the strongest early predictor of graduation. Lifetime CE dilutes the early signal with later bot-wash. Locking CE at trade-10 and trade-30 gives a frozen, non-manipulable quality stamp.

initial_ce_10.interpretation: Average SOL per trade in the first decisive 10 trades. A graduating token with 10 early trades each contributing ~0.01 SOL = raw 0.01 = norm 0.10; a token with decisive 0.10 SOL/trade avg = norm 1.0.

edge_case_fewer_than_10_trades.behavior: Use current vSolInBondingCurve / totalSwapCount as a proxy (same as capital_efficiency_raw). Signal is PROVISIONAL and lower-confidence. Do NOT gate execution on it alone.
edge_case_fewer_than_10_trades.formula: if vSolAfterTrade10 === 0: initial_ce_10_raw = vSolInBondingCurve / max(totalSwapCount, 1); else: initial_ce_10_raw = vSolAfterTrade10 / 10

edge_case_fewer_than_30_trades.behavior: Use current vSolInBondingCurve / totalSwapCount as proxy (same fallback). Initial_ce_10 should be finalized first.
edge_case_fewer_than_30_trades.formula: if vSolAfterTrade30 === 0: initial_ce_30_raw = vSolInBondingCurve / max(totalSwapCount, 1); else: initial_ce_30_raw = vSolAfterTrade30 / 30

composite_formula.description: Weighted blend of the two frozen snapshots. CE30 gets higher weight because 30 trades gives a more statistically stable estimate while still being 'early'.
composite_formula.when_only_ce10_is_final (10 <= totalSwap: initial_capital_efficiency = norm_ce10  (use single finalized signal, ignore unfinal ce30)
composite_formula.when_fewer_than_10_trades: initial_capital_efficiency = capital_efficiency_normalized  (fall back to lifetime CE — identical computation — as placeholder)
typescript_pseudocode: const ce10Raw = ctx.vSolAfterTrade10 > 0 ? ctx.vSolAfterTrade10 / 10 : ctx.vSolInBondingCurve / Math.max(ctx.totalSwapCountLifetime, 1);
const ce30Raw = ctx.vSolAfterTrade30 > 0 ? ctx.vSolAfterTrade30 / 30 : ctx.vSolInBondingCurve / Math.max(ctx.totalSwapCountLifetime, 1);
const normCe10 = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, ce10Raw / CE_SCALE));
const normCe30 = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, ce30Raw / CE_SCALE));

signal_2_accumulation_shape.rationale: A token that shows front-loaded vSol then plateaus has snipers who dumped. Steady linear accumulation signals retail. Accelerating vSol signals viral momentum. We quantify using second-derivative sign of the vSol series.
signal_2_accumulation_shape.approach: Two-component blend: (A) convexity of vSol series (second derivative sign), (B) coefficient of variation of vSol increments (organic randomness vs bot uniformity).

component_A_convexity.name: shape_convexity
component_A_convexity.description: Second derivative of vSol over the observation history. Positive = accelerating (good). Negative = front-loaded/decelerating (bad). Zero = linear.
formula_steps: Let H = accumulationShapeHistory (sorted by timestamp, length N).
Compute increments: delta[i] = H[i+1].vSol - H[i].vSol  for i = 0..N-2
Compute second diffs: d2[i] = delta[i+1] - delta[i]  for i = 0..N-3
Interpretation: mean_d2 > 0 → acceleration (signal > 0.5), mean_d2 < 0 → deceleration (signal < 0.5), zero → 0.5
component_A_convexity.SHAPE_SCALE_ACCELERATION: 0.002 SOL per 5s interval (i.e. 0.024 SOL/min² acceleration). This means a 'maximum acceleration signal' requires ~0.002 SOL/interval² increase in accumulation rate. Tune empirically.

component_B_cv_of_increments.name: shape_cv_score
component_B_cv_of_increments.description: Coefficient of variation (std/mean) of vSol increments. LOW CV = bots buying uniformly (bad). HIGH CV = organic/viral buyers of varying size (good).
formula_steps: Using same delta[] from component A.
Filter to only positive deltas (exclude intervals where vSol decreased — sells).
CV_TARGET = 1.2  — at CV ≥ 1.2 we consider this fully organic
component_B_cv_of_increments.interpretation: CV < 0.2 → very uniform (bot-like, score near 0). CV ~ 1.0-1.5 → organic (score near 1). CV > 1.2 → score clamped at 1.
component_B_cv_of_increments.CV_TARGET_rationale: For a Poisson-like organic buy stream, CV of trade sizes is typically 0.8-1.5. Bots tend toward CV < 0.3.

typescript_pseudocode: const deltas = H.slice(1).map((p, i) => p.vSol - H[i].vSol);
const d2 = deltas.slice(1).map((d, i) => d - deltas[i]);
const mean_d2 = d2.reduce((s, v) => s + v, 0) / d2.length;
// Component B: CV of positive increments
const mean_p = pos.reduce((s, v) => s + v, 0) / pos.length;
const std_p = Math.sqrt(pos.reduce((s, v) => s + Math.pow(v - mean_p, 2), 0) / pos.length);
const accumulation_shape = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, 0.55 * shape_convexity + 0.45 * shape_cv_score));

signal_3_early_buyer_composition_trend.direction: higher = composition improving (more organic retail, less bot-like)
signal_3_early_buyer_composition_trend.rationale: Paper §5: Non-bot buyer fraction > 30% at any vSol level boosts graduation. The trend matters more than the snapshot — increasing organic ratio signals viral retail uptake. Decreasing ratio = bots front-ran, retail exited.
signal_3_early_buyer_composition_trend.note: True bot detection (instruction account inspection) is pending from MEV engineer. This signal uses two orthogonal proxy metrics available NOW from TradeDataPoint fields.

proxy_metric_A_timing_regularity.name: timing_regularity_organic_score
proxy_metric_A_timing_regularity.description: Bots submit transactions at highly regular intervals. Humans are irregular. CV of inter-arrival times between consecutive early buys is our proxy.
proxy_metric_A_timing_regularity.rationale: MEV bots often fire at ~400ms intervals. Sandwich bots are even tighter. Organic buyers span seconds to minutes.

proxy_metric_B_trade_size_cv.name: size_dispersion_organic_score
proxy_metric_B_trade_size_cv.description: Bot batches tend to use uniform trade sizes. Organic buyers use highly variable sizes.

instantaneous_organic_score.description: Point-in-time estimate of how organic the buyer pool is. Blend of timing and size CV.

trend_computation.description: We bucket earlyBuyerTimingHistory into sequential windows of BUCKET_SIZE=10 trades each. Compute organic_score per bucket, then fit a linear trend across buckets.
steps: If buckets.length < 2: early_buyer_composition_trend = organic_score_t (no trend available yet)
cv_timing_i = CV of inter-arrivals within b_i (or CV of timestamps vs global mean if only 1 trade in bucket)
cv_size_i = CV of solAmounts within b_i
Fit linear regression: organic_i = a + b*i  over i = 0..buckets.length-1
trend_score: positive slope = improving composition, negative = degrading
SLOPE_SCALE = 0.10 per bucket (i.e. 0.10 increase in organic score per 10-trade bucket = full positive signal)
Trend modifier: trend_modifier = trend_normalized * 0.40 + 0.30  (maps [0,1] → [0.30, 0.70], avoiding full zeroing on bad trend)
Note: * 2.5 rescales since base * trend_modifier is at most ~0.70. Tune this multiplier empirically.
Simpler form: early_buyer_composition_trend = clamp(0.60 * base + 0.40 * trend_normalized, 0, 1)
typescript_pseudocode: const std = Math.sqrt(arr.reduce((s,v) => s + Math.pow(v-mean,2),0) / arr.length);
// Instantaneous organic score from all early buys
const interArrivals = H.slice(1).map((p,i) => p.timestamp - H[i].timestamp).filter(d => d >= 0);
for (let i = 0; i < H.length; i += BUCKET_SIZE) buckets.push(H.slice(i, i + BUCKET_SIZE));
const bInterArrivals = b.slice(1).map((p,i) => p.timestamp - b[i].timestamp).filter(d => d >= 0);
const varI = organicPerBucket.reduce((s,_,i) => s + Math.pow(i-iMean,2),0) / n;
const early_buyer_composition_trend = Math.min(1, Math.max(0, 0.60 * organic_score_t + 0.40 * trend_normalized));
// Edge case: fewer than 3 early buys

edge_cases.single_bucket: Return organic_score_t (no trend available, just instantaneous)
edge_cases.all_same_timestamp: Inter-arrival CV = undefined → treat as 0 (bot-like). Set cvTiming = 0.
edge_cases.zero_mean_sizes: Pathological — all trades were 0 SOL. Return 0.

rationale: capital_efficiency_normalized stays dominant (≥ 0.30) — it's the lifetime quality signal
initial_capital_efficiency gets 0.20 — paper says early window is the most predictive single metric
efficiency_trend drops from 0.25 → 0.15 — trend still matters but early ICE captures a better version of the same insight
curve_fill_rate_normalized drops from 0.20 → 0.15 — fill rate is velocity, ICE is quality; both needed but balanced
accumulation_shape gets 0.10 — shape is a refinement of efficiency_trend, moderate weight
early_buyer_composition_trend gets 0.08 — valuable but proxy-based until MEV engineer delivers true bot detection; bump to 0.12-0.15 when real labels arrive
large_trade_fraction stays 0.06 — still a useful raw signal
median_trade_size_normalized drops to 0.03 — mostly captured by ICE and large_trade_fraction
NOTE: After MEV engineer delivers bot detection, move 0.05 from capital_efficiency_normalized to early_buyer_composition_trend
